newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: New Zealand economy out of trough - Peters.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand economy out of trough - Peters.

text.p: New Zealand Deputy Prime Minister and Treasurer Winston Peters said on Sunday he thought the New Zealand economy had come out of its trough.
"Figures show the economy troughed in the last six months of last year, but the March year annualised for 1997 proves higher than that," he told Reuters Financial Television.

Asked about additional government spending measures, he said: "There will be no great economic impact in the adverse sense that you might be suggesting. We expect to announce greater surpluses for the next three years than the National Party government could have."
In a wide-ranging interview that was one of his first since taking New Zealand's top financial post, Peters described himself as a "thoroughly frugal" treasurer.

Regarding New Zealand's strong dollar, he said: "It's not the level of the dollar but the velocity of its rise. We appear to have arrested the velocity... And moreover, we have enabled the reserve bank governor to keep his independence but give a wider band" to more smoothly manage monetary policy.

Asked about the impact of a rising current account deficit on New Zealand's currency, Peters said: "You have to examine the components of the reserve bank concern at this point in time, but I'm not very concerned about it, and nor would it appear are markets."
New Zealand's reserve bank has projected the country's current account deficit will approach six percent of GDP within the coming years.

Peters, who has been critical of a wide-open policy on foreign investment, said: "Foreign investments should be working in the interests of the host country and local population in terms of employment, expanded growth, productivity and new technology.
"Where all of these conditions are met, this country would welcome that foreign investment," he said.
Peters was in Cebu for a meeting of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum finance ministers.

They issued a joint statement at the end of their sessions endorsing measures to encourage the international flow of investment funds, but leaving it up to individual members as to whether and when to follow through on implementation.
New Zealand is one of APEC's 18 member economies.
